title: Protein Complex Jigsaw: from typed evidence to inspectable assembly, variant perturbation and misassembly
description:
Protein Complex Jigsaw (PCJ) is an exact, inspectable framework for reasoning about protein-complex assembly from heterogeneous evidence. It keeps physical contacts, temporal prerequisites, exclusions, observed subcomplexes, alternative structural models and contextual weights distinct, then enumerates admissible seed-anchored histories or general merger trees under explicitly declared constraints.

Version 4.0.0 introduces the Protein Complex Jigsaw name and preferred pcjigsaw namespace while retaining backward-compatible scijigsaw imports and command-line aliases. It adds variant-to-mechanism perturbation analysis and an evidence-gated failure/misassembly layer. Productive assembly failure is not treated as evidence of aggregation; off-pathway outcomes are reported only from explicit provenance-bearing rules. The release also retains the exact enumeration, support queries, probabilistic extensions, structure extraction, cryo-EM observation-set analysis, hypothesis navigation, educational tools and manuscript-reproduction workflows developed in earlier versions.

Software accompanying Liò & Liò, Protein Complex Jigsaw: from typed evidence to inspectable assembly, variant perturbation and misassembly (2026, manuscript submitted to PLOS Computational Biology).
